files.role: Compact relative-byte, row and leaf-item coordinates for structural mini-block pages; nested repetition-index interpretation.
files.limits: Every physical line read in bounded untruncated outputs. Source-only analysis; no repository build/test/runtime. Parent primitive and Arrow scalar modules read only in specified contextual ranges. Caller invariants and possible panics are source deductions, not reproduced failures.
ranges: Documentation describes compact prefix sums, optional row counts and absolute base offsets. Imports supply BooleanBuffer storage and cache sizing. PrefixSums has U32 and U64 vector variants. Although declared pub, this module is private in primitive.rs; these are implementation APIs, not externally reachable through a public module path.

from_deltas selects U32 iff caller-supplied total fits u32, reserves num_chunks+1 and starts at zero. U32 casts each delta and adds without checked arithmetic; U64 also adds unchecked. Count and final total are debug assertions only. Incorrect declared totals/counts can truncate, overflow or construct inconsistent data in release.

from_prefix is private. Nonempty and first-zero requirements are debug assertions; final prefix value (or zero) chooses representation. No monotonicity or intermediate bound checks occur. U32 conversion casts every element and allocates; U64 retains input. Empty release input can become an empty prefix vector.

get and get_pair direct-index; get_pair reads adjacent starts with one enum match. num_chunks subtracts one from vector length; delta subtracts starts. Caller must provide valid lengths, indices and monotonic values. Public enum construction can bypass helper assumptions within the containing module boundary.

find excludes the terminal total, partitions starts strictly below value, returns exact first match or predecessor. Equal duplicate starts choose the first zero-width chunk, as the test confirms. It does not reject out-of-range values: beyond total selects the last start; empty or invalid prefixes can underflow. Documentation saying containing chunk needs this duplicate-start qualification.

ItemCounts distinguishes uniform values_per_chunk plus last_chunk_values from per-chunk base-two logs plus last count. Private get uses byte-index num_chunks to recognize final chunk, otherwise uniform count or 1u64<<logs[i]. No local bounds, nonzero chunk count or valid shift check; final log is unused.

RowMapping separates UniformFlat counts, Flat value-start prefixes and Nested row-start prefixes, trailer bits and leaf ItemCounts. Nested row counts include a trailer start but exclude an incoming preamble. Row count and leaf-value count are different coordinates.

RowMapping DeepSizeOf counts zero children for UniformFlat, prefix children for Flat, and row prefix plus ceil(trailer bit length/8) plus item-count children for Nested. Boolean accounting is logical bit length, not allocation capacity or shared-context deduplication.

MiniBlockChunkIndex owns base_offset, byte prefix and row mapping. new validates nothing. num_chunks comes from byte prefix. byte_range adds relative starts to base unchecked. items_in_chunk uses byte chunk count for final uniform/nested item count, or Flat prefix delta; it does not reconcile independent row/byte counts.

find_chunk on UniformFlat divides row by values_per_chunk, casts to usize and clamps to RowMapping num_chunks-1; zero stride/count can panic/underflow and an out-of-range row clamps. Other variants use prefix find. first_row multiplies index by uniform stride unchecked or direct-reads prefix.

rows_in_chunk uses byte chunk count for UniformFlat final count; Flat/Nested subtract row prefixes. Nested preamble is previous chunk trailer (false at index zero), trailer is current bit. Flat variants return false without index validation. Separate coordinate lengths are caller invariants.

cfg(test) row_mapping_debug returns exact named diagnostic shapes. new_nested_for_test parses repetition rows and supplies placeholder eight-byte chunks and uniform one-value counts; it is not a real-file index constructor.
MiniBlockChunkIndex DeepSizeOf sums byte-prefix and row-map children; base scalar has no heap child.

parse_nested_rep consumes little-endian u64 words using stride words per chunk. num_chunks floors (bytes.len()/8)/stride; zero stride divides by zero, stride one can overlap words then overrun, and trailing bytes/incomplete groups are not locally rejected. Only first two words per group are read: ends and partial. has_trailer=partial>0; starts=ends+trailer-previous_trailer; accumulate starts into prefix and set trailer bit. Arithmetic unchecked, deeper-level words ignored, and no final-trailer, row total or cross-axis count validation. Caller comment about divisible-by-eight alone is insufficient for stride one. Empty input with positive stride yields prefix[0] and empty bits.

Tests define a RefBlock and reconstruct row starts/counts using the same arithmetic on typed u64 words. This cross-representation comparison is not an independent semantic oracle. rep_bytes writes little-endian fixture words.
Prefix tests cover U32 deltas2,3,5 total10, selected getters/counts, and U64 for a single delta u32::MAX+1. They do not cover exact threshold, invalid totals, empty prefix or overflow behavior.
find test uses starts[0,5,5,12]: values3,5,11,0 map to chunks0,1,2,0. The exact duplicate chooses chunk1 even though its width is zero.

Nested parser comparison iterates four stride-two fixture sequences, asserting row start, rows, trailer and derived preamble against reference arithmetic. Four local test functions total; no local malformed-stride/length, count mismatch, all accessor or release-invariant tests. No unsafe, I/O or runtime configuration in this file.

files.role: Structural constant-page encoding, scalar/level initialization and cache loading, selected-row level extraction and Arrow materialization.
files.limits: Every physical line read in bounded untruncated outputs. Source-only analysis; no repository build/test/runtime. Parent primitive and Arrow scalar modules read only in specified contextual ranges. Caller invariants and possible panics are source deductions, not reproduced failures.
ranges: Imports connect scalar helpers, rep/def serialization, DataBlock materialization, three-slot initialization and parent-private structural page contracts. This module is public, but most implementation types and methods are private or crate-internal.

crate-internal encode_constant_page accepts scalar, serialized levels and page identity. try_inline_value decides inline bytes; otherwise encode_scalar_value_buffer frames scalar buffers. Metadata records definition meanings and optional inline bytes. Validation of scalar shape is delegated; local row/count/type consistency is not checked.

If either level Option is Some, even an empty buffer, output reserves both repetition and definition slots, using empty bytes for the absent one. External scalar gives [value,rep,def], inline gives [rep,def]. With neither level, external gives [value], inline gives no buffers. Levels clone u16 storage then reinterpret bytes. EncodedPage carries supplied counts and Structural encoding.

CachedConstantState holds scalar ArrayRef and optional u16 repetition/definition buffers. DeepSizeOf adds Arrow reported buffer memory and two bytes per level, ignoring the Context and shared-allocation deduplication/capacity. Erased Arc conversion returns self.
ScalarSource is Inline(Vec<u8>) or ValueBuffer(index). ConstantBufferLayout stores scalar source and optional rep/def byte ranges, defining a single consistent buffer-slot interpretation.

ConstantPageScheduler stores type, meanings, maximum repetition/visible levels, buffer layout and optional cache state. Constructor counts list meanings then casts to u16; max_visible_level is delegated. Inline bytes are copied. Positions plus sizes form ranges using unchecked addition.

Accepted layouts: inline with zero buffers, inline with two rep/def buffers, external with one value buffer, external with three value/rep/def buffers. Inline with other counts is InvalidInput. Zero-sized rep/def buffers become None; external value buffer remains a required scalar range even when empty.

No-inline zero buffers is missing scalar InvalidInput; two is ambiguous InvalidInput; other unexpected counts rejected. Constructor stores state with no cached data. It does not decode/validate inline bytes, array length, level counts/values, alignment or file bounds.

StructuralPageScheduler init_layout returns exactly three optional semantic slots: scalar, repetition, definition. init_from_buffers returns a boxed future with the trait method borrow lifetime, checks three-slot conversion and matches scalar source with supplied scalar buffer. Inline requires no scalar buffer; external requires one; mismatches are Internal. I/O argument is unused.

Initialization decodes inline scalar or framed external scalar, maps provided rep/def Bytes through LanceBuffer alignment2 into u16 buffers, and returns Arc<CachedConstantState>. No local level-size/count/meaning validation. This future does no additional I/O and does not install returned cache state into the scheduler.

try_load downcasts erased cached data to exact CachedConstantState, rejecting other types as InvalidInput. It checks scalar Arrow data type equals scheduler type, with both types in the error, then stores state. It does not revalidate scalar length, levels, meanings or cache-key identity.

schedule_ranges sums unchecked end-start, unwraps cached state and constructs one ready PageLoadTask with cloned shared scalar/levels, owned range queue and zero row/level cursors. Calling before try_load panics. Empty ranges still produce a task. I/O argument is unused; all data was initialized earlier.

ConstantPageDecoder owns range queue, row/level cursors, original scheduled row count and shared cached arrays. drain_ranges removes or splits queue fronts until requested rows collected. Over-drain unwraps empty queue; reversed ranges underflow. Zero-row drain returns empty. Mutation is eager with no rollback.

take_row with repetition requires cursor in bounds and rep[cursor]==max_rep, else Internal; scans until next max_rep or EOF. Without repetition it uses one level. With definitions it counts entries <=max_visible_level, directly slicing corresponding levels (short buffers can panic); otherwise all positions visible. Other repetition values are not range-checked. Successful call advances both cursors.

skip_to_row advances only forward by parsing each skipped row. Decreasing or overlapping ranges are not rejected or rewound, so correct scheduling requires sorted nonoverlapping row ranges. Cost includes skipped levels from cursor to next range.

drain first consumes queue ranges, then skips/parses rows, accumulates visible leaf values and merges adjacent selected level spans. Errors can leave queue and cursors partly advanced. It returns a task sharing scalar/levels and owning span list. num_rows reports original scheduled count, not remaining count. decoded_bytes is not overridden, so parent trait default applies.

DecodeConstantTask holds source scalar/levels, selected spans, level meanings and visible count. slice_levels allocates exact summed selected lengths and copies each selected segment; absent levels remain absent. Sum and slice bounds are unchecked.

materialize_values returns typed empty array for zero values. Empty Struct is special-cased to new_empty_fields. Other values allocate num_values UInt64 zero indices and Arrow take of scalar index0; memory cost includes eight bytes per index plus output, so constant encoding does not imply constant-memory decoding. num_values casts to usize and scalar length assumptions remain.

Decode task copies selected repetition/definition levels, recomputes visible count from copied definitions when present, materializes scalar values, creates DataBlock through from_array and RepDefUnraveler with meanings/count. Parent reconstruction applies null/nested structure. No direct decode validation flag is accepted here.

One local test constructs UInt8 scheduler using empty inline bytes without decoding them, then passes Boolean cached scalar and asserts InvalidInput mentions both types. No local complete constant roundtrip, range ordering, pre-load scheduling, empty/all-null or repetition corruption test. Empty-Struct decoder branch alone does not prove current writer emits it. No local unsafe blocks.

files.role: Dictionary-null normalization, invalid physical null-key repair and opportunistic structural dictionary encoding for fixed/variable-width value blocks.
files.limits: Every physical line read in bounded untruncated outputs. Source-only analysis; no repository build/test/runtime. Parent primitive and Arrow scalar modules read only in specified contextual ranges. Caller invariants and possible panics are source deductions, not reproduced failures.
ranges: Imports support eight Arrow dictionary key families, borrowed-byte keys, typed buffers, block statistics and take. Public constants specify128-bit dictionary fixed-width branch and32-bit signed indices. The constant128 is not a restriction on all encoding:64-bit values are also supported.

normalize_dict_nulls_impl downcasts to DictionaryArray<K> or Internal. If dictionary values contain no nulls it returns original ArrayRef without examining keys. Otherwise build old-to-new optional key mapping, removing null dictionary entries while retaining order and every valid entry, including unused entries.

For each valid dictionary value, old_idx-skipped converts to K::Native or Internal. High unused entries can fail narrow-key conversion. Logical null keys stay null; nonnull keys convert to usize or Internal then directly index mapping, potentially panicking on invalid positive index. Entries pointing to removed values become null keys. Arrow take uses generated valid u64 indices with bounds checks disabled; DictionaryArray::new constructs normalized output. No deduplication of equal values. All-null values produce empty dictionary with null keys.
Public normalize_dict_nulls dispatches Int8/16/32/64 and UInt8/16/32/64. Unsupported dictionary key type returns NotSupported including type; nondictionary returns Internal including data type.

clear_out_of_range_null_keys_impl returns original when no key null buffer or empty dictionary (there is no valid replacement index). It checks physical null slots for negative/unrepresentable or >=dictionary-length keys. If any are bad, rebuild logical keys: all null slots become physical zero while validity is preserved and values Arc is shared; otherwise return original. try_new may reject other invalid keys. This protects later null-bitmap removal for nonempty dictionaries.

Parent-module-visible clear_out_of_range_null_keys dispatches the same eight key families and uses contextual NotSupported/Internal errors for unsupported/nondictionary input. It is not a public crate entry point.

Generic variable-width dictionary helper borrows block bytes, typed offsets and U8SliceKey map entries. Stat MaxLength must exist and be a UInt64 array; expect panics otherwise. Initial payload capacity is saturating32*max_length, at least1024, then bounded by source data and target budget. Indices reserve declared num_values. No complete offset-count/first-zero/final-end validation.

Iterate every physical adjacent offset pair; conversion to usize, descending offsets or end beyond data return None. Nonzero first offset or unused trailing data are accepted. Exact byte strings map to first-seen signed i32 IDs. New entry requires positive max_entries, current unique count below it and below i32::MAX. Payload is extended before output-offset conversion and size checks, so rejected attempts still allocate transiently.

After each index, estimated encoded size is saturating payload bytes +4*index count +offset-width*(unique count+1). Return None only when greater than max_encoded_size, allowing equality. This is an output-size filter, not peak-memory bound: map, preallocation, stats and allocations before checks are excluded. No loop iterations bypasses this in-loop size check.

Successful variable-width result has dictionary offsets/data and unique count with matching32/64 offset width, plus FixedWidth indices with32 bits and declared input num_values. Statistics are recomputed for both. Physical window count is not compared with declared num_values, so malformed blocks can yield inconsistent counts.

Public dictionary_encode returns Option, not Result. FixedWidth64 interprets physical bytes as u64, allocates map, up to1024 initial dictionary values and declared-count indices, then processes every physical value. Raw-bit equality preserves float NaN payload and signed-zero distinctions rather than numeric equality. Entry caps match variable helper.

64-bit branch assigns first-seen IDs, checks saturating unique*8 +indices*4 against target after append and permits equality. Builds dictionary width64/countunique and indices width32/countdeclared, computing stats. Physical buffer count versus declared count is assumed, not checked.

128-bit branch mirrors64-bit using u128 and16 bytes per unique, constant DICT_FIXED_WIDTH_BITS_PER_VALUE=128 and32-bit signed indices. TODO for256 bits is unsupported behavior, not implemented capability. Random HashMap iteration does not determine output order; first insertion does.

Other fixed widths return None. VariableWidth supports bits_per_offset32 via u32 and64 via u64; other widths return None. Other DataBlock variants, including nullable/all-null/dictionary blocks, return None. No built-in ratio threshold/version gate/I/O: caller chooses whether to attempt and supplies caps.
High-cardinality u128 test creates120 unique values with ample entry cap1000 and original-byte budget, expecting None. It checks rejection only, not exact allocation or threshold equality.

Low-cardinality u128 test creates120 values with three distinct values, expects Some and asserts block kind, widths and counts. It does not assert exact dictionary order, indices or decoded roundtrip.

High-cardinality string test uses120 unique strings and max_entries10, expecting None. Despite naming/comment about benefit, entry cap can be the rejection reason; do not attribute it solely to byte savings.
Low-cardinality string test uses120 entries/three distinct strings and entry cap100; asserts Some and kind/counts only, not exact offsets/bytes/indices or roundtrip.

Invalid variable-width16-bit offset block returns None. String budget test uses10000 rows/50 unique values, asserting None at one-tenth original size and Some at full original size. These assertions are source evidence, not executed results.

String max-entry test uses10000 rows/200 unique values, rejecting cap10 and accepting500. Seven local test functions total; no local normalization, null-key repair,64-bit encoding, all-null/empty, exact-budget equality or malformed-count coverage. No unsafe, async or environment configuration in this file.
